documents.content:
# OFFICE OF THE CORONER — AUTOPSY REPORT
**Deceased:** Claude "Sax" Beaumont, 41
**Location of examination:** Velvet Lounge stage wing, Midtown
**Date:** Friday night, recovered 23:05

## Findings
One projectile: a .38 caliber slug recovered from the left chest, entered through the stage-wing door panel, consistent with a shot fired at point-blank to mid range from inside the wing.

## Time of death
Liver temperature and gastric contents place death between **22:30 and 22:35**.

## Notes
The victim's watch shows 22:31. No defensive wounds. The weapon was not in the room when the body was discovered. The stage-wing door was **locked from the inside** and forced open at 22:50 by Miss Kline.
documents.title: Coroner's Report

documents.content:
# STATEMENT OF MAX DELACROIX, 52
**Occupation:** Bandleader, the Velvet Lounge
**Taken by:** Det. Inspector R. Calloway, Saturday morning

> **Q: Your evening with Mr. Beaumont, Mr. Delacroix.**
> We had words at 22:10, yes — he was shorting my band's cut again. I told him in so many words I'd play my set whether he liked it or not. I walked off the stage at 22:12.

> **Q: What then?**
> The band hit the stage at 22:15 for the second set. I was up there every second until the lights went down at 23:00. The whole club watched me — forty musicians' rivals, every one of them saw me.

> **Q: Did you touch the man?**
> I told him he'd die poor. I did not touch him. Check my set log — I never left the risers.
documents.title: Interrogation — Max Delacroix

documents.content:
# STATEMENT OF VERA KLINE, 27
**Occupation:** Chorus girl, the Velvet Lounge
**Taken by:** Det. Inspector R. Calloway, Saturday morning

> **Q: Where were you when Mr. Beaumont was killed, Miss Kline?**
> In the kitchen, with Remy Fontaine. We were counting the tip jar together, from about 22:20 until the doorman let me out. He was counting coins and muttering about the new count sheet Mr. Beaumont had posted that morning.

> **Q: The kitchen door?**
> The doorman locked it from the outside at ten-seventeen, I asked him to, so no one would bother us. I was inside until he opened it at 22:47. Remy was there the whole time — I could hear him counting.

> **Q: Did you see Mr. Beaumont that night?**
> In the bar, early. He looked at me the way a man looks at a debt he refuses to pay. Nothing more before ten o'clock.
documents.title: Interrogation — Vera Kline

documents.content:
# THE VELVET LOUNGE — BAR TAB LEDGER & DOOR LOG, FRIDAY
**Source:** Bar tab book (kept by the barman) and doorman's log. Recovered by Det. Inspector Calloway.

## Doorman's log
| Time | Entry |
|------|-------|
| 22:17 | Kitchen door locked from outside, per Miss Kline's request. |
| 22:47 | Kitchen door opened. Miss Kline exits. Mr. Fontaine follows. |

## Bar tab book
| Time | Entry |
|------|-------|
| 21:58 | Whiskey (no ice) — bar — MAX D. |
| 22:05 | Two gin ryes — table 7. |
| **22:31** | **Whiskey (no ice) — bar — R. FONTAINE.** Barman's note: *"Face was white. Asked twice where the master kept the dressing-room key."* |
| 22:34 | Club emptied by closing bell; last patrons out by 22:40. |

**The kitchen door was locked from the outside at 22:17 and opened only at 22:47. Whoever was inside it at 22:31 could not have been at the bar.**
documents.title: Bar Tab Ledger & Door Log

documents.content:
# SCENE REPORT — STAGE WING & DRESSING ROOM
**Taken by:** Det. Inspector R. Calloway, 23:40 Friday

## Stage wing
Body of the deceased face-down beside the riser stairs. The wing door was **locked from the inside** — a thumb-turn only reachable from the wing side, now forced open at the frame. The .38 that fired the fatal shot was **not present**.

## Dressing room
Victim's coat and watch (stopping at 22:31) on the rack. His personal .38 revolver, normally kept in the top drawer, is **gone**. The drawer shows no forced entry. The top-drawer key is held by the victim and by the bookkeeper, Remy Fontaine — per the key log on file.

## Observations
- No sign of a struggle; the victim appears to have known his killer.
- A torn page, half burned in the kitchen stove, bears the heading **"LEDGER — FOUNTAIN"** and the words **"FRIDAY 23:00 SHOW — AUDIT PUBLIC. IT IS OVER."**
documents.title: Crime Scene — Stage Wing & Dressing Room

documents.content:
# SEALED EVIDENCE — THE LEDGER & LOCKER RECORD
**Opened by order of the Inspector, Saturday 11:00**

## The ledger
Ten years of the Velvet Lounge's books, re-totaled by the office: **$14,200** of house money passes through the bookkeeper's column and never reaches the bank. Entries were balanced each Friday night — a task no one else in the house knows how to perform.

## The locker
Locker 9 (R. FONTAINE) — opened 23:05 by the doorman, per the key log, **by the bookkeeper himself** after the death was announced. Contents: the victim's .38 revolver, the victim's top-drawer key, and a fresh page of the audit sheet in the victim's handwriting:

> *"Friday 23:00 show — announce the audit in front of the whole room. Fontaine is finished. — C.B., Thursday 21:15"*

## Assessment
The victim intended to expose the bookkeeper's embezzlement at the 23:00 show. The bookkeeper could not survive that announcement. He killed the man who would ruin him, and hid the murder weapon in the one locker only he could open and search.
documents.title: Sealed: The Bookkeeper's Ledger & Locker

stages.description: The coroner has fixed the hour: 22:30–22:35. Vera Kline says Fontaine was with her in the locked kitchen the whole time. The doorman's log and the bar tab book tell a colder story. Pin the lie to a record.
stages.objective: Break the bookkeeper's alibi. Remy Fontaine swears he was locked in the kitchen with Vera Kline from 22:17 to 22:47 — but the records disagree. Show where and when the alibi falls apart.
stages.title: The Locked Kitchen Lie

verificationRubric.criticalContradiction: Fontaine's alibi places him inside the kitchen — locked from the outside at 22:17 and opened only at 22:47 — yet the bar tab book shows him at the bar buying a whiskey at 22:31, squarely inside the time of death window (22:30–22:35). A man cannot be locked in the kitchen and standing at the bar at the same minute.

stages.description: Beyond the broken alibi lies a motive in plain ledger lines: the victim was about to expose ten years of stolen money in front of the whole room. The weapon, the key, the handwriting — every thread ends in the same locker.
stages.objective: Name the true culprit, the method, and the motive. The sealed ledger and the locker record settle who killed Claude Beaumont, how, and why he had to be silenced.
stages.title: The Ledger Speaks

verificationRubric.criticalContradiction: Fontaine embezzled $14,200 over ten years and could not survive the victim's public audit announced at the 23:00 show. Motive, means (the victim's .38 and top-drawer key — the bookkeeper held a copy), and opportunity (the 22:31 bar visit, minutes inside the 22:30–22:35 death window) all converge on him; the revolver and drawer key were later hidden in his own locker.

suspects.role: Bookkeeper — ten years keeping the lounge's ledgers

synopsis: Claude "Sax" Beaumont, the loudest voice in Midtown's jazz scene, was found slumped in the stage wing at half past ten, a .38 slug through his chest. His band was mid-set when he fell. The night belongs to the lounge's keeper of books — and his ledger keeps a different story.
title: Death at the Velvet Lounge

victim.description: Midtown's most famous crooner — and a man who owed no one.
victim.name: Claude Beaumont
victim.occupation: Jazz singer and owner, the Velvet Lounge
